brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Three cells side by side, each holding a bin (three bins in a row).
requirements.evidence: Three piece bases at cells (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0) in a straight row, each with a hex-bin-full-drain bin. Two joint bolts lock the pieces so they do not slide apart; check_build shows no LOOSE_BODY warning and meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Each of the three bins is filled with soil, so it can hold herbs.
requirements.evidence: get_build soil list shows all three bins filled to rim.

requirements.requirement: Each bin has a drainage feature (a drain or bolt-on drain bin) so water can leave it.
requirements.evidence: Each bin is the 'Bin, full depth, drained' part (hex-bin-full-drain). The configurator checks fit only; it cannot confirm the drain holes work in the printed material.

requirements.requirement: Herb plants are planted in the soil of the bins.
requirements.evidence: Three basil-young plant props, one in each bin's soil, with no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL warning.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three connected base pieces in a row, each with a full-depth drained bin, filled with soil and planted with basil. Two joint bolts lock the row. check_build is clean (meshClash clear, no prop warnings). Drainage is the drained bin variant as offered; whether it drains in practice is not checkable here.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
